title: 4-round AES-128: Normalized multiset membership distinguisher

target.description: Four inner AES rounds include MixColumns in every round; local round numbering starts0. Standard AES schedule is included among the fixed-key cases.

success.description: Derived fixed-table distinguishing-advantage lower bound for the complete normalized-multiset membership test on one 256-input delta-set and one fixed output-byte position l. Fix the complete table T0 of at most2^184 representatives generated by the source normalization X1,0^0=0, independently of the oracle. Accept if the multiset relative to at least one of all256 observed reference positions is in T0; a single arbitrary reference tested against T0 is insufficient. Observation4 supplies AES-side acceptance1 because the canonical reference occurs among those positions. For an ideal random permutation on Q=2^128 blocks, condition on a fixed reference output; the other255 outputs are sampled without replacement. Any fixed ordered vector of255 projected XOR-difference bytes has probability at most (Q/256)^255/(Q-1)_255; any fixed multiset after removing the forced zero has at most255! such orders. Union over the fixed table and all references gives false-positive probability at most 2^192*255!/256^255*product(j=1..255)(1-j/Q)^-1 < 2^-171. Indeed255!<2^1676 and product(1-j/Q)>=1-32640/Q>1/2. Thus Adv>=1-2^-171. This counts actual ideal-permutation transcripts, not an iid wrong-key approximation, the disputed journal Poisson profile, an empirical percentage, or balanced classification success. There is no search over output-byte positions. Unreported time, memory and preprocessing remain unreported. This loose bound is a new source-derived counting inference, not a number printed by the authors.

review.scope: Verified source canonical-table construction, complete 256-input experiment, all-reference membership mapping and finite-population counting inequality against the stated ideal random permutation. Independent source-first and endpoint review. This does not certify the separate disputed journal wrong-key estimate, unknown resource costs, attack implementation or a new full-paper audit.

components.description: Observation4: with the specified reference normalization and the complete source table, the AES four-round multiset belongs to the enumerated set. This is AES-side membership, not random-permutation rejection or distinguishing advantage.
